source: arXiv:2604.18821 — Evaluating Structured Strategy Backtests: Peer Benchmarks, Regime Timing, and Live Performance. Chang Liu (U. Trento / Resonanz Capital). April 20, 2026.
title: Strategy backtest live-performance haircut formula: subtract 5pp per σ of pre-launch regime extremity
rationale:
This paper studied 1,726 commercially distributed structured strategies from ten global institutions and quantified the gap between marketed backtests and live performance. Key findings:

- Raw performance gap: 2.1pp (6-month) to 3.1pp (12-month) decline from backtest to live
- After peer-benchmark adjustment: pro-forma coefficient collapses ~75-81%. Most backtest alpha is the common factor regime, not strategy-specific skill.
- Regime-timing channel: strategies launched after hot market conditions experience 4+pp worse live decay per quintile of regime extremity
  - Cold quintile: +0.8% slight improvement
  - Hot quintiles Q4-Q5: -3.5% to -4.5% decay
- Risk deterioration: MaxDD worse in 54% of live periods; Sortino worse in 59%

Actionable formula introduced by the paper:
  Expected live return = Backtest return - (5pp × regime_extremity_z_score)
  where regime_extremity_z_score = how many standard deviations above historical average the market conditions were at backtest time.

Application to George's strategy library:
- R28 PEAD Quality Filter (Sharpe 9.03, backtested 2018-2024): heavily bull-market period. Regime z-score likely +1.5 to +2. Expected live Sharpe likely 9.03 × (1 - 0.10 to 0.15) = ~7.7-8.1. Still exceptional.
- R29 Pairs (Sharpe 1.38): residualization makes it more regime-robust. Haircut likely smaller.
- Div Raise >=10% (Sharpe 4.40): long-only strategy, higher sensitivity to regime. Haircut estimate: 10-20%.
- Rule of thumb: ALL backtest Sharpe numbers should be discounted 10-20% for live deployment, PLUS the 5bp/trade friction buffer from arXiv:2603.20319.

This complements the MRP (Minimum Regime Performance) heuristic from arXiv:2604.08356 — MRP asks 'what happened in the worst historical regime', while this paper quantifies the prospective bias from the regime at launch time.
content:
### Regime-timing haircut for marketed backtests (arXiv:2604.18821)
- LESSON: Marketed backtests predominantly reflect the common factor regime at the time of backtest construction, not portable strategy-specific alpha. 75-81% of pro-forma outperformance evaporates after peer-benchmark adjustment.
- LESSON: Practical haircut formula: Expected live return = Backtest return − (5pp × regime_extremity_z_score). A strategy backtested during a strong bull market (z-score ~+2) faces ~10pp live deterioration. Apply on top of the 5bp/trade friction buffer (arXiv:2603.20319).
- LESSON: Risk metrics also deteriorate live: MaxDD worse in 54% of strategies, Sortino worse in 59%. Do not treat backtest risk numbers as reliable floor estimates.
- LESSON: Cold-regime launches perform slightly better live (+0.8%); hot-regime launches -3.5% to -4.5% by quintile. Our 2018-2024 backtest window is a predominantly warm/hot regime for US equities. All George Sharpe estimates should be deflated 10-20% before deployment decisions.
- WHEN: Evaluating any strategy for live trading eligibility. Reviewing rounds 28-35 results. Setting position sizing for live deployment.
- SOURCE: arXiv:2604.18821 (Chang Liu, U. Trento / Resonanz Capital, April 2026). 1,726 strategies, 10 global institutions. Journal of Asset Management (under review).
